To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the α9β1-integrin accelerates cell motility through binding of SSAT, which catabolizes spermidine and spermine to enhance Kir channel function.
the α9 integrins accelerate cell migration through binding to spermidine/spermime acetyltransferase, a polyamine-modifying enzyme.
the α9 integrins accelerate cell migration through binding to SSAT, which in turn enhances migration through polyamine-mediated modulation and regulation of Kir4.1/2 ion channels.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism of cell migration and the role of the α9β1-integrin in cell migration.
the molecular mechanisms of cell motility.
the mechanisms by which the α9β1 heterodimeric integrin stimulates cell migration.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
α9β1 enhances cell migration by SSAT-dependent catabolism spermidine and spermine, which results in the inhibition of Kir4.1 and 4.2 channels.
the α9β1 subunit of the integrin family of cell adhesion molecules enhances cell migration through binding to the polyamine metabolizing enzyme, spermidine/spermime acetyltransferase.
the α9 integrins stimulate cell migration through the modulation of Kir4.1 and Kir4, 2 channels.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
α9β1 enhances cell migration by localized SSAT-dependent catabolism spermidine and spermine and subsequent Kir4.2 activation.
the α9β1-integrin enhances cell migration through binding to the polyamine catabolic enzyme spermidine/spermime-N1-acetyltransferase (SAT) and the subsequent catabolism (acetylation) of polyamines.
the α9β1-integrin enhances cell migration through polyamine catabolic enzymes that are localized to focal adhesions and that modulate Kir channel activity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the α9β1-integrin enhances cell migration through polyamine-mediated modulation and inhibition of inward-rectifier Kir channels.
the α9 integrins can stimulate cell migration through a novel pathway involving spermidine and spermine catabolism.
the α9β1 subunit enhances cell migration by modulating polyamine-mediated Kir channel activity.
